html:
The Nansemond are an Algonquian people of the Nansemond River, a branch of the James River in southeastern Virginia. Their name means "fishing point".

Around 1600 they were part of the Powhatan paramount chiefdom, with neighbours such as the Chesapeake and the Warraskoyack. They fished, farmed maize and gathered oysters. Soon after Jamestown was founded in 1607, colonists raided their towns and burned their fields, and the English took their land through the 1600s.

One branch became Christian through marriage with a colonist in 1638, and its descendants stayed in the area. The Nansemond gained federal recognition in 2018 with five other Virginia tribes.
sum: The Nansemond are an Algonquian people of the Nansemond River, a branch of the James River in southeastern Virginia. Their name means "fishing point".
